 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the appellant under Section 4 of the High Court Act, challenging the order dated 06.12.2023 passed by the learned Single Judge in W.P.No.203259/2023.
2.
Brief facts of the case are that, the appellant is the owner of the land bearing Sy.No.53/3 measuring 15 acres 11 guntas situated at Halladkeri (K) village, Taluka and District Bidar.

The further case of the appellant is that on 20.03.2023 without any notice or information to the appellant, respondent Nos.3 and 4 equipped with the heavy earth moving machines, trespassed into the appellant's land bearing Sy.No.53/3 on its Southern border and destroyed the old compound wall and put a pandal on the encroached area and erected a hording on the land declaring Bhoomi Pooja ceremony for the proposed construction of Ganesh Visarjana Platform in the encroached area belonging to the appellant.

Immediately, he made representation not to demolish and cause NC:
2024:KHC-K:2236-DB interference.
Since the same was not adhered, the appellant had filed W.P.No.201789/2023.

This Court by order dated 07.08.2023 has disposed of the writ petition with liberty to file representation before the competent authority, directing that if such representation filed, the authorities to consider the same.
Since the authority has not considered the representation, the appellant has again approached this Court by filing another writ petition in W.P.No.203259/2023.
This Court by order dated 06.12.2023 has dismissed the writ petition reserving liberty to the writ petitioner to approach the appropriate forum for redressal of his grievance.
Being aggrieved by the same, the Writ Petitioner has filed this writ appeal.

3. Sri J. Augustin, the learned counsel appearing for the appellant has contended that respondent Nos.3 and 4 herein without authority of law has encroached property belongs to the appellant and without giving any notice, they have put up pandal for proposed construction of Ganesh Visarjana Platform.
This action of the respondents NC: 2024:KHC-K:2236-DB is without authority of law.
He further contended that the appellant's land has been encroached without acquisition as provided under Land Acquisition Act and without paying any compensation.
Without considering this aspect of the matter, the learned Single Judge erred in dismissing the Writ Petition.

4. Per contra, Sri.Viranagouda M. Biradar, the learned Addl. Government Advocate appearing for the State contended that the State has not encroached the property of the appellant on the other hand the appellant has encroached the property of the State.
Therefore, this Court has rightly deserved that the dispute between the parties is in civil nature and it has to be dealt before the appropriate forum by filling a suit.
Hence, he sought for dismissal of appeal.

5. In reply, the learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that even though if there is a dispute with regard to question of facts this Court under Article 226 of Constitution of India can decide on the basis of the NC: 2024:KHC-K:2236-DB affidavit filed by the parties.

In support of his contentions, he has relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Smt.
Gunwant Kaur and others vs Municipal Committee, Bhatinda and others reported in AIR 1970 SC 802.
6.

Therefore appellant again filed the writ petition in W.P.No.203259/2023 with following reliefs.
a). Issue an order or a writ in the nature of Mandamus by directing the respondents not to encroach in to the Land of the Petitioner Sy.No.53/3 of village Halladkeri (k)

Land Sy.No.52 of Village Halladkeri (k) and to have access to the Construction site by adopting due process of the Law as envisaged in Sec 82 of The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation And Resettlement Act 2013.
b) And further be pleased to direct the respondents to restore compound wall of the land Sy.No.53/3 of village Halladkeri, Tq & Dist. Bidar, which is destroyed by them during the Month of March 2023.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In this case the appellant except producing rights of records, no other documents have been produced to prove his title over the property in dispute.

Even before the learned Single Judge the learned High Court Government Pleader appeared for the State has specifically contended that there is no encroachment made by the State or the authority and the land in dispute is belongs to the Government.

Since there is a dispute regarding encroachment of the land, the learned Single Judge has rightly dismissed the writ petition reserving liberty to the appellant-Writ Petitioner to approach the appropriate forum for redressal his grievance.

Even though judgment relied by the learned counsel for the appellant in Smt. Gunwant Kaur (supra) the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that if question of fact is complex nature, the High Court in Writ Petition may decline to entertain the Writ Petition at para-14 it is held as under:
"When the petition raises questions of fact of a complex nature, which may for their determination require oral evidence to be taken, NC: 2024:KHC-K:2236-DB and on that account the High Court is of the view that the dispute may not appropriately be tried in a writ petition, the High Court may decline to try a petition.

Rejection of a petition in limine will normally be justified, where the High Court is of the view that Dr Robert Michael Miranda vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159588160/
4 the petition is frivolous or because of the nature of the claim made, dispute sought to be agitated, or that the petition against the party against whom relief is claimed is not maintainable or that the dispute raised thereby is such that it would be inappropriate to try it in the writ jurisdiction, or for analogous reasons."

sentences.text: Since there is question of facts of complex nature, this Court under Article 226 of Constitution of India cannot decide the issue as it requires evidence of the parties.
Therefore, learned Single Judge has rightly dismissed the writ petition.
There is no error or illegalities in the order passed by the learned Single Judge.
Hence, we decline to interfere with the impugned order Accordingly, the writ appeal is dismissed.
In view of the dismissal of main appeal, pending IAs, if any, do not survive for consideration and same stand disposed of.
